opusRecommendation:
## One change: ship one verifiable end-to-end release

Deploy commit `34a867d`. Then record and publish a single continuous demo, under 3 minutes, on that deployed build. Release the audited MIT package alongside it.

## Why it matters

Presentation (5.5) is your weakest score. The current 96-second video omits the payment approvals and captures, so judges cannot see the most differentiated part of the product. Showing the full flow in one take supports Presentation, Design and Technological Implementation. Disclosing limits honestly also protects credibility.

This will not reach 80/90 alone. Potential Impact and Innovation still need real nonprofit-staff feedback, and the AI drafting result remains a loss (11/24 vs 14/24 baseline). Do not tune prompts to flip that gate.

## Acceptance test

- The hosted Render build reports commit `34a867d`.
- The full test suite on the release package has 0 failures.
- A fresh clone of the public package passes the same suite.
- The public video shows, uncut:
  - pause/restart
  - the sponsor capture and donor refund
  - goal clarification
  - three MCP quotes
  - exact-plan approval
  - PayPal sandbox buyer approval
  - both captures, with provider readback showing COMPLETED and the configured payee
  - signed-receipt verification and tamper detection
- A persistent on-screen "PayPal sandbox, test funds" label is visible throughout.
- A closing card states the limits: project-controlled suppliers, shared demo PIN, no user study, AI has not beaten the baseline, Donorbox/Givebutter overlap.

## Plan

1. Finish the release audit. Deploy and verify the commit hash. Warm the instance to avoid a free-tier cold start during recording.
2. Script the flow in about 150 words. Do a dry run, then record in a single take.
3. Add captions and the limits card. Upload the video publicly and link the repo and video in Devpost.
4. If time remains, run brief walkthroughs with real nonprofit staff. Report their feedback verbatim and add no claims beyond it.
